Akut Barn er et sundhedsfagligt opslagsværk, der hjælper autoriserede sundhedsfaglige personer til hurtigt og sikkert at begynde indledende behandling af akut syge eller tilskadekomne børn.

Akut Barn indeholder tre dele: 

 1. Guideark med hurtigt overblik over vitalparametre, størrelser af udstyr og doser af udvalgt medicin til akutte situationer for et barn med den valgte vægt 
 2. Behandlingsvejledninger for 29 akutte, livstruende pædiatriske tilstande samt vejledning i generel ABCDE-vurdering og smertebehandling og sedation af børn. Vejledningerne er tilpasset den valgte vægt og dækker minimum de første 30 minutter af behandlingen
 3. Genoplivningsalgoritmer for stabilisering af nyfødte samt avanceret genoplivning af børn fra hhv. Dansk Pædiatrisk Selskab og Dansk Råd for Genoplivning

Alt indhold er tilgængeligt for børn i intervallet 3-50 kg.

Akut Barn er let og intutiv at anvende:

 - Ved at dreje på hjulet på forsiden af Akut Barn vælges alder og vægt. Når der trykkes ”OK” midt på hjulet, præsenteres guideark svarende til den valgte vægt
 - Behandlingsvejledninger tilpasset den valgte vægt præsenteres ved at trykke på menu-knappen ”Akutte tilstande” øverst på guidearket
 - Genoplivningsalgoritmer er tilgængelige direkte fra forsiden ved klik på hhv. baby-ikon og børne-ikon.
 
Akut Barn er ikke en erstatning for lokale vejledninger men kan hjælpe behandlingsteamet hurtigt i gang og kan mindske risikoen for medicineringsfejl i akutte situationer. Anvendelse sker på eget ansvar.

Akut Barn er udviklet af ansatte ved Rigshospitalets Afdeling for Bedøvelse, Operation og TraumeCenter:

 - Overlæge Morten Bøttger, børneanæstesiolog
 - Overlæge Lasse Høgh Andersen, børneanæstesiolog og præhospital akutlæge 
 - Overlæge Michael Friis Tvede, anæstesiolog og præhospital akutlæge

Det faglige indhold er udviklet i samarbejde med en gruppe af eksperter i akutbehandling af børn både præ- og inhospitalt.

Akut Barn 2022 er udviklet på baggrund i midler afsat af regionsrådet i Region Hovedstaden til Børneparat samt økonomisk støtte fra Rigshospitalets Afdeling for Bedøvelse, Operation og TraumeCenter. Akut Barn 2022 er en videreudvikling af den første version af Akut Barn, der blev udgivet med støtte fra TrygFonden i 2012.

Denne appen er for deg som trenger hjelp eller gjennomgår behandling ved Reproduksjonsmedisinsk avdeling på Rikshospitalet og Ullevål sykehus. I denne appen finner du viktig informasjon om infertilitet, diagnose og behandling, hvordan du søker og annen informasjon. For å få et best mulig samarbeid, ber vi deg lese informasjonen i denne appen og kontakte oss hvis noe er uklart.

The ReSound Smart 3D app lets you control your hearing aids directly from your mobile device. You can change programs, and make simple or more advanced sound adjustments and save them as favorites. The app helps you learn what you can do and how to do it. It can even help you find your hearing aids if you lose them. Last, but not least, you can have your hearing care professional update your hearing aid programs and send you new hearing aid software without taking a trip to the clinic.

Notes: Please contact your local ReSound representative for product and feature availability in your market. We recommend that the hearing aids run the latest software version. If in doubt, please contact your hearing care professional.

Please consult the ReSound app website for up-to-date compatibility information: www.resound.com/compatibility 

Use the ReSound Smart 3D app to: 
•	Enjoy optimization anywhere with ReSound Assist: Request help with your hearing aid settings from your hearing care professional and receive new settings and software updates. 

And use these direct control and personalization options:
•	Adjust volume settings on your hearing aids
•	Mute your hearing aids
•	Adjust volume of your optionally acquired ReSound streaming accessories
•	Adjust speech focus as well as noise and wind-noise levels with Sound Enhancer (feature availability depends on your hearing aid model and the fitting by your hearing care professional)

The ReSound Tinnitus Relief™ app uses a combination of sounds and relaxing exercises that aim to distract your brain from focusing on tinnitus.  Over time the brain learns to focus less on the tinnitus. 

The app lets you manage your personal library of soundscapes to be used for sound therapy, one of the most common therapies to minimize the effects of tinnitus. Either listen to the default soundscapes of create your own from a collection of environmental sounds and small pieces of music. 

To help you cope with your tinnitus, Relief also provides different activities to relax and get better sleep such as guided meditations, breathing exercises and imagery.

The Learn section will teach you more information about what is tinnitus, what are the causes of tinnitus, common therapies as well as tips to help you better deal with the effects of your tinnitus.

My Relief will help you to create a personalized plan to teach you manage your tinnitus. Just answer some questions about your tinnitus and the issues that bother you the most, and ReSound Tinnitus Relief will create a weekly plan to help you train managing your tinnitus.

Tinnitus suffers often also have some degree of hearing loss, so we added a hearing test for all users to get a quick hearing test result directly in the app and guidance on what to do next, in case a hearing loss is detected.

Just download ReSound Tinnitus Relief and listen to it as you normally listen to music from your smart phone. 

The app is a tool for anyone who has tinnitus. It should be used in combination with a tinnitus management programme or plan set up by a hearing care professional.

The Mariners Medico Guide is a medical app designed explicitly for seafarers and the maritime industry. When downloading the app, you can access free, up-to-date, easy-to-use medical guidance on your mobile device or desktop. Giving you the ability to search for support at sea (offline) 

Guidance is structured by symptoms and includes visual support for simple step-by-step medical procedures, as well as advice on when and how to get expert medical advice from a maritime telemedical assistance service – TMAS or Medico.

Key features 
* Written by specialists in maritime medicine
* Continuously updated
* Fast access to guidance in common emergencies
* Fully indexed information about diseases and injuries
* Information on medications generally found in the ship’s medicine chest
* List of medical equipment often needed onboard

The app is Flag State approved by the Norwegian Maritime Authority as an equivalent national publication to the WHO International Medical Guide for Ships (IMGS). Other flag states recognise the app as a more up-to-date maritime medical guide which may be substituted for the IMGS.

The information in this app is intended to provide general guidance to enhance the knowledge of medical treatment of seafarer’s onboard ships. The app does not provide medical advice for treatment of specific conditions presented by specific individuals. The information contained in the app is for information purposes only, it is not professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. It is not intended to replace professional medical advice. The user should never delay seeking professional medical advice and treatment recommendations from a medical professional.
